thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH: runtime oom + gpu fragmentation on pool-03 — paging observed, impacting ~3 customers. Pager: jamie (oncall). Please respond.

jamie (oncall): I'm on it. Confirming affected hosts and scope.

lee (pager): seeing elevated OOMs on runtime nodes rtm-03.*, eviction spikes around 14:12 UTC. Requests are hitting 503s for some tenants.

jamie (oncall): timeline start 14:09 UTC — first error spike in metrics. Can someone pull recent `nvidia-smi` and dmesg?

sanai (eng-runtime): grabbing logs now. Pasting quick `nvidia-smi` snapshot and dmesg tail:

```
# nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv
memory.used [MiB], memory.total [MiB]
15360 MiB, 16384 MiB
15872 MiB, 16384 MiB
15360 MiB, 16384 MiB
```

```
[  14:11:23 ] oom-killer: Out of memory: Killed process 4217 (runtime_worker)
[  14:11:23 ] slab_reclaim: order:0..., fragmentation: high
[  14:11:26 ] GPU memory page fault, migrating pages
```

sanai (eng-runtime): Also grabbing KV cache metrics from /var/log/rtm/kvcache/stats.log — high resident set and swap activity.

"kevin (customer-success):" *Customer impact:* two mid-tier customers saw increased 503s for chat generation from ~14:10–14:25 UTC. One reported degraded latency but no data loss.

rachel (sre): Noted CPU load and page-in spikes on the host. Looks like KV cache growth + larger batch sizes caused memory pressure. Has anyone recently rolled a model variant or changed default batch_size?

lee (pager): We pushed a routing config change at 14:05 that increases max_batch_size=8 for some SaaS tenants (intended to improve throughput). Might be correlated.

sanai (eng-runtime): Hypothesis A: increased batch_size -> larger per-request KV cache/activation working set -> fragmentation / page-in -> OOM. Hypothesis B: suboptimal slab allocation on driver with certain allocation patterns causing fragmentation even at 90% free memory.

jamie (oncall): Running mitigations now: 1) rollback batch_size to 4 for affected tenant routes via feature-flag, 2) trigger KV cache trim on pool-03, 3) fallback routing to smaller model variant (redwood-small) for heavy tenants. Executing step 1.

ops-bot: feature-flag rollback applied: route:r/tenant-42 max_batch_size set to 4 — applied to pool-03 nodes.

sanai (eng-runtime): Triggering `kvcache purge --pool pool-03 --threshold 0.6` to free prefetched prefixes.

ops-bot: kvcache purge job queued (job-id: purge-23560001).

rachel (sre): Observing memory telemetry after rollback and purge. Preliminary: page-in rate dropped 70% within two minutes, swap usage stabilized, no new OOMs in last 4 minutes on the affected hosts.

lee (pager): Customer 42 latency back to normal by 14:21 UTC. Customer 17 still seeing occasional 503s — might be on a different host.

sanai (eng-runtime): Collecting deeper memory maps and runtime allocation traces. Uploading tarball to s3: s3://redwood-incidents/2356000001/rtm-03-memory-traces.tar.gz

jamie (oncall): Good. Please annotate timeline in the thread so we have in-incident RCA artifacts. I'll coordinate handoff to postmortem owners.

sanai (eng-runtime): Adding timeline bullets: 14:05 change increased max_batch_size=8 for route X. 14:09 first telemetry spike. 14:11 OOM + oom-killer logs. 14:12 rollback batch_size -> 4. 14:13 kvcache purge started. 14:16 fallback to redwood-small for heavy traffic. 14:21 customers reports service recovery. 14:30 monitoring stable.

rachel (sre): I'll capture the metric graphs (mem, swap, page_in, oom_count) and attach to the postmortem doc. Quick note: fragmentation metrics from driver show many small free segments — defrag didn't kick due to driver heuristics.

lee (pager): Hypothesis tracking (in-thread):
- H1: batch_size increase -> increased ephemeral allocations in GPU -> fragmentation -> OOM.
- H2: KV cache growth + aggressive prefetch policy -> inflated resident GPU allocations -> paging.
- H3: kernel/driver slab fragmentation exacerbated by allocation patterns -> OOM even if aggregate free memory seems available.

sanai (eng-runtime): Evidence so far: after batch_size rollback and kv purge, memory pressure reduced quickly (supports H1/H2). Also seeing `gpu_mem_map` with lots of small free ranges -> supports H3. We'll instrument a trace of allocation sizes on next deploy.

kevin (customer-success): I've messaged the two impacted customers with a brief summary and ETA for postmortem (EOD). Customers asked if this will recur — being transparent about change that likely triggered it.

jamie (oncall): For live mitigation notes: 1) Keep batch_size conservative on pool-03 until quantization profile updated. 2) Add a short-circuit that routes to smaller variant when page-in rate exceeds X. 3) Temp disable aggressive kvcache prefetch for affected tenants. I'll add to runbook.

rachel (sre): Agreed. I'll also add an automated alarm: if page_in_rate per-GPU > 100/s and swap > 1GB within 5 min, send high-priority alert and throttle batch_size automatically.

sanai (eng-runtime): We should add a guard in runtime: monitor effective working set per-request and refuse batch growth that would push working set > threshold. Will prototype as a microchange.

lee (pager): One more thing — customer traces show that larger prompts plus function-calls combo created very tall KV caches. We should add a per-tenant soft-limit on cached prefixes.

ops-bot: purge-23560001 completed. freed ~3.2GB GPU resident per node.

sanai (eng-runtime): Post-mitigation verification: ran `nvidia-smi` diff, memory used dropped ~2.5GB avg per GPU. No new OOMs in 20m.

jamie (oncall): Handoff: I will create postmortem doc and assign owners: eng-runtime (sanai) lead for root cause analysis, sre (rachel) for detection/alerts, product/ops (kevin) for customer comms.

kevin (customer-success): Requested a short timeline + TL;DR to customers by EOD. I'll coordinate with product.

sanai (eng-runtime): To-do list for RCA: collect full allocation traces, reproduce with reduced harness (batch=8, kv-prefetch enabled), test driver defrag heuristics, experiment with quantization/activation cache sizing.

rachel (sre): I'll draft alerting thresholds and add an oncall playbook snippet describing rollback steps and kvcache purge command sequence.

jamie (oncall): Closing live thread once postmortem doc exists. Thanks everyone for quick coordination.

lee (pager): Thanks — leaving handwritten notes in postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged as resolved for now. Severity: Sev2 -> monitoring. Please file postmortem with timeline and follow-ups.

sanai (eng-runtime): Uploading additional logs: s3://redwood-incidents/2356000001/alloc-traces.log and s3://redwood-incidents/2356000001/kvcache-metrics.csv

kevin (customer-success): Marking impacted customers: tenant-42, tenant-17. Noted that tenant-42 had highest error rate.

jamie (oncall): final note: we'll schedule a retro to decide whether default batch_size should be lowered cluster-wide or tuned per-hardware profile.

rachel (sre): Adding action item: instrument per-request working-set metric in telemetry (owner: eng-runtime).

sanai (eng-runtime): Acknowledged. I'll start a branch with guards and a perf test to evaluate.

kevin (customer-success): I'll update customers after the postmortem is published.

jamie (oncall): closing in 10m unless anything else pops up. Great job triaging quickly. :thumbsup:
